diagram_math_checks.objects: All integration variables x,x_0,...,x_r lie in the original measurable state space (E,mathcal E); initial x has law mu.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement line 30 integrates mu(dx); def-initial-distribution-of-a-markov-chain identifies mu=L(X_0). Each K^m is a probability kernel E x mathcal E -> [0,1] by def-iterated-transition-kernels.

diagram_math_checks.relations: Arrow x -> x_0 is K^{n_0}; x_0 -> x_1 is K^{n_1-n_0}; the final arrow into x_r is K^{n_r-n_{r-1}}. All arrows point chronologically rightward. The ellipsis abbreviates the intervening observed-state chain, possibly empty, rather than a further random coordinate.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These are exactly the first, second and final kernel integrals of the Statement. thm-chapman-kolmogorov-equations gives E[f(X_{m+n})|F_m]=K^n f(X_m), and proof step 1.1 uses exactly these positive time gaps.

diagram_math_checks.relations: Factors f_0(x_0), f_1(x_1), f_r(x_r) attach to the corresponding observation times n_0,n_1,n_r; omitted factors are explained in prose.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The Statement integrates a product of tests at each successive coordinate; proof step 1.1 defines G_j=f_j K^{n_{j+1}-n_j}G_{j+1}, confirming placement.

diagram_math_checks.relations: For n_0=0 the first arrow is Dirac evaluation, including x_0=x; r=0 and r=1 retain the appropriate initial portion. No deterministic map, independence claim, or extra commutativity relation is asserted.
